packs.title: USA, 1 December 2026
packs.summary: Four funded PhD applications close on Tuesday 1 December 2026 (Hopkins Epidemiology, Emory Epidemiology, Pittsburgh IBGP, Yale public health), with Hopkins GDEC and a Columbia MPH as optional extras. This pack gives the verified requirements from the official pages, the letters plan and a dated timeline from 9 November.

blocks.note: All four main deadlines are Tuesday 1 December 2026, US Eastern. Official pages arbitrate; items below marked 'not found' were not stated on the official pages read.

blocks.h: Hopkins Bloomberg PhD Epidemiology (SOPHAS)
ul: **Deadline:** submit by 1 Dec 2026; supporting documents (letters, transcripts, evaluation) no later than two weeks after the deadline (official rule). Cycle opened 12 Aug 2026.
**Fee:** $155 first programme, $65 each additional. International waiver exists but must be requested before you submit; once approved you have 14 days to submit and it covers the first $155 only.

**Letters:** 3 required (Epi FAQ: at least one academic, an advisor preferred; may mix academic and professional). Trap: SOPHAS can show the file complete with 2, but Bloomberg still requires the third.

**Statement:** statement of objectives and research goals. The Epi FAQ states a **two-page limit** (earlier notes said none; corrected). The generic how-to-apply page gives no limit. CV/resume required. No adviser needed in advance; faculty may be named.

**Credential evaluation is mandatory** for international coursework: WES ICAP course-by-course through SOPHAS, or ECE course-by-course sent to Bloomberg. **ECFMG certification is not accepted.** WES ICAP costs **$239** (the $80 coupon applies if the SOPHAS waiver is approved), plus delivery fees. WES's clock starts only when documents are accepted; the evaluation then takes about 1-2 weeks; door to door 4-6 weeks.

**English (scores under 2 years old):** TOEFL iBT **100 for scores before 21 Jan 2026; 5.0 on the new 1-6 scale for scores after 21 Jan 2026** (a test taken now uses the new scale); IELTS Academic 7; Duolingo 130; PTE 68. Waiver only if a WES or ECE evaluation verifies English as the sole language of instruction for the bachelor's/professional degree; the waiver cannot apply until the evaluation is received. Medium-of-instruction letters are not accepted. Duolingo/PTE scores go directly to BSPH Admissions Services.

**Work experience (conflict inside JHU):** the programme page lists one year of full-time work in a related field as required; the Epi FAQ calls one year of full-time post-baccalaureate work only 'strongly recommended' for ScM and PhD. Whether the internship year counts is not stated. Email BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu.
**GRE:** not required and not reviewed.

**Submit-early caveat:** SOPHAS lets you submit before transcripts and recommendations arrive, but it will **not review or verify the application until all transcripts, payments and recommendations are received**. Allow up to 10 business days of SOPHAS verification.

blocks.h: Emory Rollins PhD Epidemiology (LaneyConnect)
ul: **Deadline:** final deadline 1 Dec 2026 (deadlines fall at midnight US Eastern). **Fee:** $75 (waivers exist per notes).
**Letters:** 3, from people familiar with your academic performance.

**Statement of purpose, 500 words:** previous research experience or training, research interests, how the programme addresses them, long-term goals. Plus the Statement on Building Collaborative and Respectful Graduate Communities (500 words) and an optional diversity statement.
**Name at least two Epidemiology graduate faculty** you want to work with. CV/resume required.
**Transcripts:** upload scanned registrar-issued transcripts (web printouts not accepted); non-English transcripts need notarized translation. Official transcripts only after admission.

**Credential evaluation (conflict, ask):** the programme and Laney pages do not make it mandatory (Laney: international applicants 'may want to consider' one). But the general Rollins how-to-apply page says international applicants must use WES, and that page covers all degrees including the SOPHAS MPH. Ask Epi admissions before relying on 'no WES'.
**English:** TOEFL/IELTS for international applicants; no numeric Epidemiology minimum found (do not borrow another programme's number). Contact the programme about the English-medium waiver.
**Stipend:** $43,260 for FY26-27 per Laney (CBA rate); the Rollins programme page still shows the stale $42,000 (2025-26). Full tuition scholarship per the Rollins page. GRE optional.
**Odds and next steps:** about 200+ applications for 10-14 places; a virtual visit day is usually a Friday in the first two weeks of February.

blocks.h: Pittsburgh IBGP PhD (lab-based biomedical science)
ul: **Deadline:** Fall 2027 application open 1 Sep to 1 Dec 2026 (no time of day stated); review is rolling and early files help. **Fee:** $50, non-refundable, due before processing; a need-based waiver was not found on the pages read (ask).
**Letters:** minimum 3; the FAQ says the research-advisor letter is very important.

**Personal statement:** required; no word limit or prompt on the pages read; the research description is heavily weighed. CV: not listed as a requirement (upload one if the portal allows). Transcripts are uploaded in the application; no WES requirement stated.

**English:** TOEFL iBT 100 (or 5 on the new scoring), IELTS 7.0, Duolingo 120; scores under 24 months old on 1 Sep of the start term. Exempt only with a bachelor's or higher from a US regionally accredited or other approved English-instructed institution ('approved' is not defined) - plan on needing a real score. TOEFL institution code 2927, dept 45.

**Academic bar:** minimum GPA 3.2 on 4.0 (incoming average 3.7); GRE not required. The degree is expected to be in a biological or physical science, mathematics, computer science or engineering; whether an MBBS fits is for the programme to judge.
**Honest weak point:** all successful applicants have research experience, most at least a year in a lab. A clinician's manuscript portfolio is the counter-argument; front-load it in the statement.
**Timeline:** interviews mostly January to March (overseas by teleconference); acceptances rolling 1 Feb to 15 Apr; offer letters mailed before 15 April.

blocks.h: Yale School of Public Health PhD (via the Graduate School, GSAS)
ul: **Deadline:** 1 Dec 2026, 11:59 pm Eastern (deadlines are subject to change). The public health PhD must use the GSAS PhD/Master's application, not SOPHAS. Fall 2027 application is open at apply.grad.yale.edu/apply. Contact: phdms.publichealth@yale.edu.
**Departments:** Biostatistics, Chronic Disease Epidemiology, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology of Microbial Diseases, Social and Behavioral Sciences, Health Policy and Management.
**Fee:** $105; US citizens, permanent residents and non-US citizens can all request a waiver.

**Funding:** all PhD students are guaranteed five years of 12-month stipend and tuition support (fellowships, teaching fellowships, traineeships, research assistantships) plus health coverage. GSAS tuition 2026-27 is $52,400 and is covered. GSAS 2026-27 minimum stipends: $52,046 (humanities/social/physical sciences) and $53,629 (biological and biomedical); the Public Health band was not stated. A $1,500 one-time relocation award is confirmed.
**Letters:** 3, entered by name in the application; letters need not arrive before submission, but review starts shortly after the deadline. **CV** required; no writing sample.

**Statement of academic purpose:** research interests and faculty; you may list up to three faculty; no mentor needed in advance. The YSPH page states no word limit; the 500-1,000 word figure in earlier notes was **not found** (check the GSAS Application Question FAQs).
**GRE:** required only for Biostatistics (PhD and MS) and Health Policy and Management (PhD); not accepted for the other four PhD departments; no waivers; self-report scores; institution code 3987.

**English (PhD):** the PhD page gives only Speaking minimums (to teach): TOEFL iBT Speaking 26+ (before 21 Jan 2026) or 5.5+ (on or after); IELTS 'speaking 8.0 or higher' as written. The 100 / 7.0 overall figures are the **MS** minimum, not the PhD. Average admitted PhD: TOEFL 106, IELTS 7.5. Duolingo not accepted. Waiver: undergraduate degree from a school where English is the primary language of instruction with at least three years in residence; no waiver based on an advanced degree.
**Transcripts:** unofficial transcripts uploaded with the application; records in English or translated; no WES requirement seen (but no explicit 'no WES' statement either).

**Eligibility and odds:** a master's is not required (some programmes prefer post-baccalaureate training); whether an MBBS counts as the bachelor's equivalent is not ruled on - email the programme. 5-year average acceptance 3% across the six departments; average admitted GPA 3.8, no minimum. Decisions mostly February to early March; reply by 15 April.

blocks.h: Hopkins GDEC PhD and Columbia MPH (optional add-ons)
ul: **Hopkins PhD in Global Disease Epidemiology and Control (found by Claude on 9 Nov, not in your notes; read on publichealth.jhu.edu):** the page says the prior graduate degree can be **"a degree in medicine, veterinary medicine, or dentistry"**, so an MBBS qualifies on its face. Prior work experience is **"not required but highly desirable"** (the Epi PhD asks for a year). Apply by **1 December** for an August start. The catch: **standardized test scores (GRE) are required**, and the department waives this only for people who already submitted official GRE scores to Hopkins' MSPH in International Health within the last 10 years. Hopkins says it reviews applications holistically. It is STEM designated (24-month OPT extension). Same BSPH PhD stipend guarantee as the Epi PhD ($52,000 minimum through June 2027, tuition, fees, medical benefits). Not checked: letters and statement rules for this programme, GRE seat availability and score-delivery time before 1 Dec. Run it through SOPHAS (one more designated programme, $65 extra if added to the Hopkins Epi application).

**Columbia Mailman MPH:** preferred deadline 1 Dec 2026 (priority review and full scholarship consideration); standard deadline 15 Jan 2027 (rolling); **1 Mar 2027 late consideration** (reviewed as space remains, scholarships subject to availability). Applies via SOPHAS; Statement of Purpose max 500 words.

**Columbia money:** merit awards $7,500-$30,000 per year; need-based grants ($10,000-$12,500) are FAFSA-based, so assume none for an international applicant; the 'PopFam $10,000' figure from earlier notes was not checked. Partial funding only (the Sakib model), not a funded PhD.

blocks.h: The letters
ul: **Count:** 3 strong letters + 1 backup referee cover all of Hopkins, Emory, Pittsburgh and Yale; the same referees serve all of them and each portal sends its own request link. MRC (27 Nov) needs 2 referees with institutional email addresses, so brief the same people about both sets of dates.

**Who:** (1) research supervisor or senior co-author (the Pittsburgh 'research advisor' slot and the most important letter everywhere); (2) a professor who taught or examined you and can rank you against other students; (3) a clinical or internship supervisor or senior collaborator; (4) a backup senior name asked at the same time.

**Briefing pack for each referee:** CV draft, SOP draft (even rough), transcript, one line on each programme, exact deadlines, and 4-5 specific things they personally saw you do (a dataset cleaned, an analysis run, a deadline saved). Generic letters are the known failure mode.
**Statements:** Hopkins research-weighted within two pages; Emory a hard 500 words naming 2 faculty; Pittsburgh research description first; Yale research interests plus up to 3 faculty.

blocks.note: 1 Dec in Baltimore, Atlanta, Pittsburgh and New Haven runs to about the next morning in Dhaka; do not plan on that buffer.

blocks.h: Honest timing note and open gates
ul: A fully **verified** SOPHAS file by 1 Dec is not achievable from a standing start in November (WES approval plus up to 10 business days of SOPHAS verification). What is achievable, and normal, is a complete submitted file with WES verification following within the two-week supporting-document window.
The risk sits with Hopkins' WES-dependent English waiver: a real test score, if you can book one, de-risks the whole round.
Open gates to resolve by email this week: Hopkins work-experience line; Emory WES (ask); whether an MBBS counts as the bachelor's equivalent at Yale; Pittsburgh fee waiver and MBBS fit.
Hopkins SOPHAS fee waiver (pack notes, not re-verified): Epidemiology is not among the departments with its own waiver.

packs.title: MRC North West PhD, 27 November 2026
packs.summary: A fully funded four-year biomedical PhD at Manchester and Liverpool, open to international applicants, closing Friday 27 November 2026 and applied for through up to two named projects. This pack lists what the official pages confirm, what is still unconfirmed (MBBS eligibility, fee) and a supervisor-first timeline.

Friday 27 November 2026 (no closing time of day stated on the page); projects and applications opened 30 Oct 2026

Tuition at the home or international rate plus a stipend at the UKRI rate for four years; international applicants explicitly eligible

blocks.note: The MRC file is project-led, not portal-led: you apply to a named advertised project (up to two, each a separate application), and contacting the supervisor first is described as one of the most important steps before applying.

blocks.h: What the application requires (official pages, re-verified)
ul: **Eligibility:** First or Upper Second-class UK honours degree (or international equivalent) in a relevant discipline, held or about to be obtained. A master's is not required, but many successful applicants have one or research experience. **Whether an MBBS with the internship still in progress counts is not stated**; ask the Doctoral Academy.
**Two projects maximum:** each is a separate application with its own tailored supporting statement. Main supervisor only is entered in the portal.

**Documents:** supporting statement; reference details; degree certificates and final or interim transcripts; official English certificates if applicable; **CV is required**. The page states: **'A research statement is not required for this programme.'**
**Supporting statement:** no specific word limit; **2-4 pages maximum recommended** (FBMH general page; earlier notes said 1-2 pages).

**References:** two references from people who know your academic ability; one may be from your clinical or work background; the referee email must be institutional, not personal. Referees receive an automatic request when you submit, and you cannot be nominated without references. (This is the FBMH general research-degree page; confirm in the portal.)

**English:** **not required at the point of application**; any offer is conditional on an approved English test (such as IELTS). FBMH general guidance: typically IELTS 6.5 overall (5.5 each component, 6.0 writing) or TOEFL iBT 90; some programmes 7.0. Tests are valid 2 years; ask whether an English-medium MBBS qualifies for a waiver.
**Application fee:** not found on the programme page; confirm in the portal before assuming no fee.

**Portal entry values (use exactly):** Level Postgraduate Research; Entry year 2027/28; Intake September (although the studentship starts October 2027); Funding: Research Council / MRC PhD Studentship / Awarded / Fully Funded.
**No WES or credential evaluation** requirement stated for this programme; do not order WES for Manchester. No GRE requirement stated.

blocks.h: Fit note and project shortlist
ul: **Fit:** this is a biomedical-science DTP and most advertised projects are lab-based. Your fit is decided by project choice, not programme title: population, clinical-data, modelling and prescribing projects are where an MBBS plus your manuscript portfolio is a strength; a wet-lab molecular project would be a weak file.

Titles below came from FindAPhD listings on 7 Nov, not the official projects list; **confirm each on Manchester's official projects page** (supervisor emails and prerequisites live there) before emailing.

**1. Rebuilding trust in vaccination: a Large Epidemic Model to predict immunity gaps** (Liverpool; Dr S Chen, Prof A J Jorgensen): best fit; your dengue and cold-mortality trend work and GBD experience map onto it.
**2. Closing the loop: AI-guided approach to prioritise competence experimentation of emerging arbovirus risk** (Liverpool): strong fit with your dengue work.
**3. Genomic and mathematical approaches for precise targeting of public health interventions to control viral emergence** (Precision Medicine DLA): strong fit.
**4. Antibiotic use in hidradenitis suppurativa: prescribing patterns, treatment trajectories and antimicrobial treatment failure** (Manchester): good fit, clinical and data-led.
**5. Personalised approaches to reduce indoor environmental exposures during pregnancy** (Manchester): good fit, exposure epidemiology.
**6. A digital portal incorporating PROMs for equity and effectiveness of outpatient epilepsy care:** good fit, health services and equity.
**7. Optimising data completeness in clinical prediction models with high-frequency patient-generated health data** (Manchester): good fit; your NHANES/GBD data work is the argument.
**8. Reliable Multimodal Agentic AI for cardiovascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction** (Manchester): adjacent fit; heavy AI-methods weight.
**Suggested pairing:** (1) + (2), both Liverpool public-health modelling; or (1) + (4) for a Liverpool and Manchester spread. Do not pair two lab-heavy projects.

blocks.h: Supervisor email template (send Mon 9 - Tue 10 Nov)
p: **Subject:** Prospective MRC NW-DMS applicant: [exact project title]. Body 150-200 words with your academic CV attached.

Content: who you are (Bangladeshi MBBS graduate, internship, Chattogram); one line naming a specific paper or project of theirs and why it matters; two lines on you (degree, one relevant skill, one result with numbers such as a submitted manuscript or dataset analysed); the connection to their project and one question showing you read it; the ask (a brief call, and is an MBBS applicant without a prior master's a realistic fit?). Close with the 27 Nov deadline.
One polite reminder after a week with no reply, then move on; a generic mass email is spotted and ignored.

packs.title: SOPHAS: fees, waiver, costs and applying mid-internship
packs.summary: SOPHAS charges $155 for the first programme and $65 for each additional one, and Bangladesh qualifies for the international waiver if you request it before submitting. You can apply during the internship, but SOPHAS will not review the file until transcripts, payments and letters arrive.

blocks.h: Fees and the international waiver
ul: **Fees:** $155 for the first programme and $65 for each additional (SOPHAS Applicant Help Center, updated 6 Aug 2026). Some programmes add a supplemental fee.

**Fund is limited:** waivers are first-come, first-served and 'can be quickly depleted'. There is no public counter; call SOPHAS customer service on **617-612-2090** before requesting. You need an account; requests by mail or email are not accepted.
**Bangladesh qualifies:** you must be a citizen of **and** currently reside in a country on the UN Least Developed Countries list; Bangladesh is on SOPHAS's own list.
**Covers the first designation only** ($155); each additional programme's $65 is still payable. One waiver type per cycle.

**$80 WES coupon:** the form also lets you request $80 off a WES course-by-course evaluation; valid for your initial WES order only, no refunds once the order is placed. WES ICAP itself costs $239 (course-by-course Basic is $186, but Hopkins requires ICAP).
**Must request before submitting.** Requests after submission are not honoured. Processing takes up to 10 business days and you cannot submit while the request is pending.

**14-day clock:** once approved you must submit within 14 days including weekends and holidays; no extensions; missing it voids the waiver and you cannot reapply. Outstanding transcripts, recommendations and scores need not arrive within the 14 days.

blocks.h: Sequencing the waiver against the deadlines
ul: Because approval can take up to 10 business days and then starts a 14-day clock, request it only when the application is essentially ready to submit, but not so late that processing eats the deadline: for a 1 Dec Hopkins deadline, a request around Tue 10 - Wed 11 Nov leaves room.
If the waiver has not been approved by about Fri 20 Nov, weigh simply paying $155 to protect the deadline.
The waiver covers one programme: use it on the most expensive-to-miss first designation and pay the $65 extras.

blocks.h: Applying mid-internship
ul: **Yes, you can apply in the final phase of the degree.** Universities require the degree completed by enrolment, not by the application date; none of the four MPH programmes checked requires work experience or internship completion for admission.

**SOPHAS mechanics:** in-progress and planned coursework is a normal part of the application. You can submit before transcripts and recommendations are received, **but SOPHAS will not review or verify the application until all transcripts, payments and recommendations arrive.**
**Emory (official FAQ):** applicants near completion may apply in their final year with incomplete transcripts; an offer is contingent on a final transcript documenting completion.

**Drexel:** 'The MPH programs do not require work experience' confirmed. The exact 'prior to enrolling' wording was not seen on the page read; it asks for a bachelor's or equivalent international degree.

**Georgia State:** 'bachelor's at the time of enrollment' was **not verified** (catalog page fetch failed). **UIC:** bachelor's in any field, GPA typically 3.00, GRE not required; 'in progress' wording not found.

**Academic Update** (2026-27 cycle): 21 Jun - 30 Jul 2027, updated transcripts by 5 Aug 2027, but it is written for US and English-Canadian coursework; for a Bangladeshi MBBS the practical update route is an updated evaluation or transcript per programme instructions, so confirm with each programme.

blocks.h: Where the realistic chances are
ul: **Admission:** MPH cohorts routinely include physicians; the screens are the degree, GPA conversion, English scores and the statement. None of the 12 lists research experience as an admission requirement. The public universities (Georgia State, UIC, USF, UAB, Albany) plus Drexel and Tulane are the realistic-admission band; Emory, Columbia, BU, GW and Brown are competitive for everyone and their top merit tiers are the long shots.

**Where Sakib-type mechanics exist:** assistantships with tuition waiver (Georgia State confirmed; UIC unconfirmed), Emory REAL (up to $3,000/semester), Drexel's research fellowship (tuition scholarship + RA), and automatic merit review at stated priority dates (Emory, Drexel, GW, UIC, Albany). USF is the counterexample: it tells internationals to arrive self-funded.

**None passes the board's hard filter** (full tuition + stipend guaranteed). Every route is partial scholarship plus work, and first-year funds must be documentable for the I-20 regardless of expected earnings.
**Sakib's own case (7 Nov talk, unverified claim):** a 50% Columbia scholarship still left a very large balance; he calls the MPH a 'cash-in' programme.
Research experience matters mainly for the top merit money and for landing RA jobs after arrival, not for admission itself.

blocks.h: Fee waiver sequencing
ul: One SOPHAS account, one transcript and WES set reused across programmes; each added programme costs $65 (UIC adds an $80 supplement, USF a separate application).

The international fee waiver (Bangladesh is on the UN LDC list on SOPHAS's page) covers only the first $155 and must be requested before submitting; approval takes up to 10 business days, then you must submit within 14 days or lose it for good.
Request it when WES is ordered and the statement is near final. Make the earliest-deadline programme your first designation.
Also use the waiver form to claim the $80 WES coupon before placing the WES order (initial order only).

blocks.h: F-1 work rules (official wording)
ul: **On campus:** no more than 20 hours a week while school is in session; full-time during scheduled breaks. You may apply up to 30 days before classes start. RA/TA/GA assistantships count as on-campus employment inside the same cap.

**CPT:** needs at least a full academic year of full-time enrolment (exception for programmes whose curriculum requires earlier training); must be integral to the curriculum; one employer per authorisation. **One year of full-time CPT eliminates OPT eligibility.**
**OPT:** 12 months per level of study, authorised by USCIS with an EAD; STEM extension (24 months) only for eligible STEM degrees.
**Off-campus work** otherwise needs one full academic year plus economic hardship. Do not plan year-1 income around off-campus work.

packs.title: What other applicants say: guidance posts and the Sakib talk
packs.summary: Summaries of social-media guidance posts and the 7 November BOB-MedElites talk by Dr Sakib, plus the status of every lead they raised. These are personal views, not official rules; the unnamed Netherlands award is now identified as the University of Twente Scholarship.

blocks.h: Building an extracurricular (ECA) profile from home (Career & Abroad, Facebook reel (Bangla), 28 Oct 2026)
ul: The reel is about building an **extracurricular-activity (ECA) profile from home**, and the title promises **15 free resources**.
No scholarship, programme, amount or deadline is named anywhere in the caption.
The list of 15 resources was **not retrieved** (Facebook gave no captions for this reel), so only the title and caption are known.
How to use it: watch the reel yourself and note the 15 items, then keep only those that fit your health, research or public-health field.
blocks.note: Caution: Only the title and caption were read; the actual 15 resources were not retrieved, so nothing here is confirmed content of the reel.

blocks.h: How to make a Europass CV for higher studies (Mrinmoy 'Moon' Modak (Graduate Research Assistant, University of Florida), Nextop USA Facebook group, long Bangla post, 1 Nov 2026)
ul: **Europass** is the EU's free online CV builder; build it only on the official site, **europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv**. You can make an account or use a guest option, then download a PDF.
It is **not mandatory** everywhere. If a university or scholarship gives its own CV format, use that. USA, Canada, Australia and UK programmes often prefer their own 2 to 3 page academic CV.

Order of sections: basic info (professional email, LinkedIn or research profile), Education (latest degree first, official degree names, CGPA if relevant, thesis title), Work experience, Research experience or projects, Publications and presentations, Skills, Languages, Awards, References.
For research roles, write what you did, how, and your own role: project title, lab or institution, supervisor, duration, objectives, your contribution, methods, analysis tools.
List publications with authors, year, title, journal, DOI and an **honest status** (Published, Accepted, Under review, Submitted). Never show an unpublished manuscript as published.
Name only skills and software you really know (R, Python, SPSS, Excel, GIS and so on). IELTS or TOEFL: give test name, score and date if relevant.
Ask referees before you put their names in; leave references out if none are asked for.
For a PhD, stress education, research experience, publications, research skills, conference presentations and research interests so a professor sees the match with their work.

Keep a folder system (Academic Documents, Transcripts, CV, Research Experience, Publications, IELTS/TOEFL, Recommendation Letters, Awards, SOP and Research Proposal) and one **master CV**, then make a trimmed version per programme.
Before sending, check spelling, degree names, dates, CGPA, email, phone and formatting, and save as YourName_Academic_CV.pdf.
blocks.note: Caution: The post is general advice by a PhD-stage student, not an official rule; always follow each university's own CV instructions. The author promises a follow-up on emailing professors.

blocks.h: Month-by-month application calendar for the Sept 2027 intake (Deshi Passport, Facebook reel with full post text (Bangla), 21 Oct 2026)
ul: **Oct to Dec (start now):** Sweden 16 Oct 2026 to 15 Jan 2027; Norway around 1 Dec; Stipendium Hungaricum expected to open in November (no official date yet); ETH Zurich and EPFL masters usually Nov to Dec (sources differ, check the university site); Charles University English medicine 30 Nov; Greece English masters Dec to May, many 31 May; Netherlands: Studielink applications open from October.

**January:** Finland 7 to 21 Jan 2027 (Studyinfo.fi); Sweden closes 15 Jan; Hungary likely mid-January (last year 15 Jan); Germany summer semester usually 15 Jan; Radboud with scholarship **31 Jan**; Comenius University Slovakia 31 Jan to 31 Mar; most Erasmus Mundus deadlines Dec to Jan.

**Feb to Mar:** WU Vienna English masters 1 Feb to 31 Mar; Denmark masters until 1 Mar (DTU 15 Jan to 1 Mar); Italy usually Feb to Apr by university; Charles University 28 Feb to 30 Apr; KU Leuven and Ghent from 1 Mar; Vilnius 1 Mar to 30 Jun; Campus France Feb to Mar.

**Apr to May:** Netherlands without scholarship usually **1 Apr** (Radboud basis), some programmes 1 May; Tartu and Tallinn 1 Apr; Latvia RSU 1 Apr to 30 Jun; Portugal Mar to Jul (apply by May to leave visa time); KU Leuven until 15 May; Greece 31 May.

**Jun to Jul:** Spain public universities May to Jul (Complutense and Barcelona 31 Jul); Germany winter semester usually 15 Jul, many earlier; Lithuania 30 Jun; Latvia 30 Jun or 31 Jul; Portugal 31 Jul. Poland has no single date; each university sets its own.
Start APS, transcripts, certificate verification and IELTS **3 to 6 months early**; a late deadline is not a reason to start late.
Visa processing takes long, especially for Germany, so leave time after an offer.
The poster's own rule: dates change yearly, so check each one on the university or official portal before you apply.
blocks.note: Caution: This is one creator's compiled calendar; the poster says dates shift each year, and the Swiss dates and the Hungary opening date are flagged uncertain in the post itself. Verify each date on the official portal.

blocks.h: The bank-statement mistake that gets Italy study visas rejected (Imran Faruk Official (education consultant), Facebook reel (Bangla), 22 Feb 2026)
ul: The commonest mistake is **fake transactions**: withdrawing and re-depositing the same money again and again (for example cycling Tk 5 lakh) so the statement looks long and busy.
The pattern the speaker warns about: keep Tk 2 to 5 lakh rolling, then deposit the real Tk 20 to 25 lakh only in the last 2 to 3 months before submitting.

Why it fails, he says: the **balance never really grows**, and turnover does not match the sponsor's salary. Example: salary Tk 1.5 lakh a month with half spent means the highest normal transaction is about Tk 2 to 2.5 lakh, not Tk 10 to 15 lakh a month.
A visa officer who sees this may reject you for dishonesty.

What to do instead: let the account follow **real life**. Pay school fees, medical bills, shopping, restaurant bills, mobile recharge, bKash transfers and family support through the bank or card, and withdraw small amounts instead of one big monthly cash withdrawal.
When 12 months of statements match your real spending and your supporting documents, the embassy is more likely to believe the whole file.
blocks.note: Caution: This is a consultant's own view of how Italian visa officers read statements, not an embassy rule; check the embassy and university pages for the actual financial requirements.

blocks.h: Skills that put you ahead for a fully funded Public Health scholarship (Dhrubo (ধ্রুব), Facebook text post (Bangla), 1 Nov 2026)
ul: For applicants with good results but **no research experience or publications**: learn technical skills now so you can show professors a usable skill set.
**Statistics software or language:** R, Stata, SPSS, Python or SAS. You do not need all; start with one and add others by work type.

**Epidemiology and biostatistics methods:** logistic regression, linear regression, survival analysis, Cox regression, meta-analysis, systematic review, sample-size calculation. Learn the ones that fit your research interest.
**Research tools:** REDCap, Rayyan, RevMan, Zotero, NVivo. Start with **Zotero**; add Rayyan and RevMan for systematic review or meta-analysis.
**GIS and disease mapping:** QGIS or ArcGIS; start with QGIS.
Aim: a stronger profile for funded graduate programmes and a clearer skills story when you write to professors.
blocks.note: Caution: General advice from a social-media post; it names no scheme, amount or deadline and does not promise funding.

blocks.h: Can you get full funding with no research experience? (Toma Rahman, Facebook reel (Bangla and English, about 2 min), 2 Nov 2026)
ul: Her answer: saying you cannot get funding without research experience would be a lie, but she has seen **people get funded with little**; those are exceptions, and most funded research masters and PhD students have some research experience, strong or weak.
Her own case: no undergraduate thesis at Dhaka University, but she worked as a **research assistant from first year**.
She also helped others with theses: **data collection, interview transcripts, data management, literature review**. She had not run her own full research.
In her application she said plainly that she had not written a thesis but had done these tasks, and wanted to learn through the thesis. She says it worked.
Her advice: try your best to get at least some research experience.
If your university cannot offer it, she says it may not be the right university for you, which she calls a harsh comment.
blocks.note: Caution: One person's experience and opinion, with no scheme named; her story shows it can work, not that it will.

blocks.h: The '50+ scholarship opportunities' list post (Bashar Gulumbe, Facebook text post, 2 Nov 2026)
ul: The post says the author compiled **50+ scholarships and funded research programmes** with deadlines from November 2026 into 2027.
The list itself is in the comments or links, and it was **not retrieved**; the post body names no scheme, amount or deadline.
Do not use the count of 50+ as a source.
If you open the list, check every scheme on its own official site before spending time or money (the same tip as in Naim's Diary, see the government-scholarship entry).
blocks.note: Caution: Aggregator teaser; nothing in it was checked, and the actual list was never seen.

blocks.h: Four student profiles with the best Italy study-visa chances (Imran Faruk Official (consultant, ends with a client pitch), Facebook reel (Bangla, auto-captions), 13 Oct 2026)
ul: **Profile 1, bachelor's applicants:** HSC GPA 4.0 or more out of 5 (or diploma CGPA 3.0 or more out of 4), **IELTS 6.0 or more**, and an entrance or CEnT-S exam pass; show about **Tk 30 to 40 lakh** with genuine transactions and proper sponsor papers. Two factors matter most: the entrance exam and bank solvency.

**Profile 2, fresh graduates (within about 1 to 3 years):** CGPA 3.3 or more out of 4, even with no job; IELTS 6.0 or more (applying on MOI alone lowers the odds); show about **Tk 25 to 35 lakh** of genuine sponsor funds, consistent with the sponsor's documents.

**Profile 3, graduated about 3 to 5 years ago:** a decent CGPA, 1 to 2 years of job experience **related to the degree**, IELTS 6.0 or more, Tk 25 to 35 lakh or more, and a perfect sponsor file. The figures in this stretch were garbled in the captions, so treat them as approximate.

**Profile 4, graduated about 5 to 10 years ago:** a moderate CGPA is fine (about 3.0 or 3.5), with 2 to 5 years of job experience, best at a multinational or reputed company and in the same field. He says some get visas on MOI, but IELTS makes it risk-free. These applicants fund themselves partly from savings and rely less on a sponsor. Figures here are also approximate.
For every profile the bank statement and the sponsor's financial papers must be **consistent and genuine**.
He says these are his own observations from several years of casework, not a rule, and that other profiles can also get visas.
blocks.note: Caution: Consultant marketing; the lakh figures and CGPA and IELTS cut-offs are one agent's experience, not Italian embassy requirements, and some figures were garbled in the captions. Check the embassy page.

blocks.h: How to get a government scholarship: the full process (Naim's Diary, long Facebook video (Bangla), 1 Nov 2026)
ul: **Step 1, analyse your results honestly.** For bachelor's applicants he says most government scholarships need HSC GPA **4.5 or more out of 5** (5.0 best). For master's applicants, CGPA **above 3.0**; a 2.8 or 2.9 can sometimes be covered by strong extracurriculars, which HSC applicants cannot do.
Lower-competition schemes exist (he gives an ICCR-type scholarship as an example, around 3.8 to 4.0) but with limited subjects.

**Step 2, organise documents.** Use a real scanner, not phone photos, with a clear folder structure. Basics: passport, passport photo, NID, birth certificate, academic documents, extracurricular proof, language certificate if any; sometimes police clearance and a medical certificate.
**Step 3, build an Excel sheet** of target schemes: name, documents needed, when the circular comes, deadline, whether IELTS or police clearance is needed, and the application link.
Examples he names: Chinese government, Stipendium Hungaricum, Russian, Kazakhstan, ICCR, Morocco, Mexican and Romanian government scholarships.

**Where to find them:** the Bangladesh ministry site he names as shade.gov.bd (as heard in the transcript, spelling unconfirmed) for ministry-routed offers, and **opportunitiescorner.com** for international ones. Then go to each scheme's own site for details, to avoid scams and mistakes.
**Step 4, apply:** register, fill the form exactly as instructed, upload documents. A few schemes add an entrance exam or interview (he cites the Russian one); most do not.
blocks.note: Caution: Aimed mainly at HSC and bachelor's applicants, so the GPA cut-offs are the speaker's rules of thumb and mostly not your level; the website names are as transcribed and should be checked.

blocks.h: What to do to win an undergraduate scholarship (Annels Scarlen Diaz, Nextop USA group, Facebook photo post (Bangla), 3 Nov 2026)
ul: Aimed at **HSC-level students**, so it is not your level; the ideas below are what the post says.
Keep SSC and HSC results strong and consistent; add subject depth through Olympiads, science fairs and projects.
Prepare IELTS or TOEFL, and for the US the SAT only where required (many universities are test-optional; check each one).
Choose a few extracurriculars and stay long enough to show real impact rather than collecting **20 certificates**.
Show leadership by starting small initiatives: free tutoring, a reading or science club, a clean-up or tree planting. Document what you did, why, and what changed.
Tailor profile, story and essays to each university; do not copy others' essays or exaggerate.
Build relationships with teachers early so recommenders can write real examples.

Research who gives financial aid to international students: full tuition or tuition plus living, separate application, SAT or ACT, deadlines, family financial papers. In the USA need-based aid and merit scholarships are different things.
Keep an Excel plan with a reach, match and safer list, and prepare essays, letters and financial papers well before deadlines.
blocks.note: Caution: Undergraduate-level advice; an attached table comparing countries was partly illegible and its figures were not used.

blocks.h: Studying in the USA with zero living cost: the Resident Assistant route (Mohammed Farhan Hossain (Bangladeshi undergraduate in Massachusetts), Facebook reel (Bangla and English), 28 Dec 2025)
ul: He arrived on a **merit scholarship that covered tuition only in part** and not living costs, which were roughly **double his tuition share**.
On seniors' advice he applied for a **Resident Assistant (RA)** post in his residence hall: a **free single room, a meal plan and a biweekly stipend**, so living cost is effectively $0.
Apply **as early as the application opens**. The pipeline is application, selection, interview, then a training class, taking **one to two semesters**.

Look for **three on-campus roles** first: Resident Assistant, **Research Assistant** (approach professors directly, before or right after arriving, saying what skills you bring), and **Teaching Assistant**.
Search on **Handshake**; build a detailed profile with a professional photo and apply early and widely.
F-1 student visa limit: **20 working hours a week**; do not exceed it, because employers can report it.
His view: use the degree years for long-term growth and skills rather than cash work off campus.
blocks.note: Caution: This is an undergraduate's personal experience; RA posts mostly serve enrolled undergraduates in residence halls and do not cover tuition, so for you it is a gap-closer (like RA or TA work for partially funded students), not a funded route.

blocks.h: Opportunities in USA as a Bangladeshi doctor (BOB-MedElites live, 7 Nov 2026)
ul: **Two myths:** that Bangladeshi doctors can only work unpaid in the USA, and that there are no scholarships for a master's. He calls both partly myth; the real gap is that students do not know the pathways (full-time job routes, visa application, funded master's) and seniors seldom guide. **Internship timing:** his internship ran Feb to Feb and he started applying in the **November before it ended**. He had felt completely lost during internship; his first research project was stuck for a year with no publication, and publications came during internship.
**Age advantage:** he says Bangladeshi doctors can start early; he is a doctor at **25**, while many people finishing medical school in the US are about **30 to 32**. He calls this a big advantage.

**Pick programmes that match your own interest and experience** (his are maternal health, HIV and adolescent health), not any scholarship in an unrelated field such as biological sciences; he says you would not get that scholarship.

**IELTS:** a minimum score is enough for selection, but a visa officer may look more favourably on an **8 than a 7**, and English speaking plays a big role in the visa. If a visa is refused, understand the real reason. He names TOEFL or IELTS as the options.

**Decide your destination early.** Prepare for the US, UK or Australia the same way at first, but pick one. On the **Middle East and Maldives** route he is blunt: little career growth, and he has seen seniors come back after about 3 years to sit **FCPS**. He says the same effort is better spent on the US route.

**US routes (his view):** USMLE, or take a position that adds to your portfolio first, then build clinical experience and Steps; he says within three years you can get into residency. Do not wait in Bangladesh to finish everything: the earlier you enter the US system, the earlier opportunities come.

**Research path for students in Bangladesh:** start with voluntary research. **Case reports in 3rd year** from atypical cases, then **cross-sectional**, then **cohort** studies (prospective cohort work is the most valuable), alongside medical life. **One hour a day, not eight.** **Build the research team:** look for **like-minded people**; attach a professor or senior who can guide the first project; learn **research methodology** from first idea to manuscript (YouTube short courses, BMSS courses). Run several projects, since only one may pay off, and it takes time.

**Avoid paid authorship:** do not buy papers, pay to be listed as an author, or use anyone who charges to publish for you. He says it is very detrimental for your career, it will come out, and people see through it.

**CV volunteering must relate to your field.** A health camp does not count if you cannot relate it. His examples: research with Public Health Foundation and BMSS, work with United Nations-linked groups (as heard), community awareness (dengue, prevention), work with vulnerable groups. Then, in his words, research, research, research and research. He had 7 years of voluntary work and 3 years of research before MBBS ended.

**Letters of recommendation matter a lot in the US.** Even with a low profile, a professor who sees your potential will write a very good letter. His suggestion: one from your principal, one from the medicine department head, one from the surgery department head. He says Bangladeshis put too little effort into this.

**Emailing professors:** he emailed about **50** professors at the universities he wanted and about **30** replied wanting a Zoom meeting; some offered research positions. Email contents: who you are in one line, interest in a specific part of their work (his example was an HIV drug clinical trial), your experience, what you want to learn, then **ask for a meeting date and time** instead of asking if they have a position. He says a professor who is convinced makes a high scholarship easy.

**Columbia story:** the scholarship needed CGPA above **3.3**, and although his MBBS marks were over 80%, he had no 3.3 CGPA. He says CGPA conversion from MBBS is of little use. He got a **50% scholarship**, which he says still left about Tk 1 crore to pay, so he wrote to the professor to ask for more. **MPH is a cash-in program** (it needs a lot of money); Emory has the second best MPH in the US in his view, Hopkins Bloomberg the first. He did not apply to Hopkins because he had a full job.

**Funded PhD:** he says a PhD costs nothing and pays about **$3,000 to $4,000 a month** for a profile like his (borderline cases possible). He says direct master's or PhD applications often get rejected and that applicants who send 20 or 30 applications blindly then complain online.

**Mindset and community:** be passionate and hungry; he says he does not charge for knowledge but wants the same hunger from a mentee and does not believe in ready-made publications. He ends by urging a stronger Bangladeshi doctor community abroad, like the Indian and Pakistani ones, and says to text him if you come to the US.
